summary: This resolution sets special floor procedures to immediately consider and pass H.R. 1908 (as amended by a substitute creating the Restore Trust in Congress Act), which bans Members of Congress, their spouses, and dependent children from owning or trading most stocks, commodities, and similar investments, requiring divestiture within set deadlines with limited exceptions and penalties.

scores.thoughts: The bill text establishes ethics rules prohibiting Members of Congress from owning or trading certain investments. It contains no provisions that authorize, appropriate, or alter any form of government spending.
The bill references existing IRC section 1043 certificates of divestiture for tax treatment of required sales but does not create, raise, lower, or modify any tax rates, liabilities, or policies.
No provisions address healthcare coverage, markets, regulation, or public programs.
No provisions relate to firearms, regulations, or gun rights.
No provisions address immigration, visas, borders, or related protections.
No provisions address abortion access or restrictions.
No provisions address military or defense spending levels.
No provisions address environmental regulations or protections.
No provisions address welfare programs, food assistance, or related benefits.
No provisions address schools, education funding, or school choice.
No provisions address drug enforcement, decriminalization, or related policies.
The bill creates civil penalties (fees and disgorgement) for ethics violations but does not engage with criminal sentencing, policing, or justice-system reform.
No provisions address tariffs, trade agreements, or protectionism.
No provisions address deficits, debt reduction, or fiscal policy.
No provisions address legal protections or rights for LGBTQ+ individuals.
No provisions address foreign aid or international assistance.
No provisions address voting access, election integrity, or campaign finance beyond a narrow restriction on using certain funds to pay ethics penalties.
No provisions address technology regulation or data privacy.
No provisions address worker protections, unions, or employer flexibility.
No provisions address religious exemptions or anti-discrimination rules.
